transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-25 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Alex (AlphaTek Eng Lead), Samir (AlphaTek CTO), Nina (AlphaTek SRE), Elena (AlphaTek Product)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run for about 45-60 minutes, goal is to scope the POC around capacity and autoscale. quick intros?
00:15 Alex: yeah Alex here, eng lead for our assistant product, we want to validate costs and the latency for our peak loads
00:30 Samir: Samir CTO, decision maker for infra and budget
00:40 Priya: Priya from Redwood, i'll focus on sizing and benchmarks, hi Maya
00:50 Maya: maya cs, will coordinate pilot logistics
01:05 Jordan: great quick agenda, baseline throughput needs, reserved GPUs vs hosted, burst approach, fallback policies, success criteria and timeline
05:12 Alex: to ground this, our current service serves requests for: short form chat (avg tokens 60) and longer context summarization (avg tokens 400) - 95% of traffic is chat tho. baseline steady qps about 25 rps, spikes to 160 for 3-6 min windows during certain events.
07:02 Nina: also memory usage on our side, KV cache per convo is about 50KB, caching strategy in our code is sticky session based
08:10 Priya: ok that's useful, so two patterns: low-latency chat (short tokens) and bursty long jobs. For POC we usually recommend reserved GPUs sized for baseline steady throughput plus a burst pool we can allocate for spikes.
09:05 Jordan: what latency SLOs are you trying to hit? both p50 and p95?
09:20 Elena: product wants p95 < 600ms for chat and p95 < 3s for long summarizations. p50 should be < 200ms for chat ideally.
10:00 Priya: good, those are achievable with the right model tier and GPU class. quick clarification: are you ok using a slightly smaller model variant during bursts if needed?
10:18 Samir: yes as long as we have fallbacks and there's an accepted regression window - product cares about quality but we can accept a 2-3% drop temporarily
11:05 Jordan: noted, fallback policy could be: reserved pool (baseline) pinned to chosen model; burst pool uses compatible quantized variant; if burst pool exhausted, fallback to lower-cost model in different region or queue requests with priority routing.
13:00 Alex: what's the cost tradeoff for reserving GPUs vs just relying on hosted burst?
13:18 Priya: reserved gives predictable unit cost and better cold-starts; hosted burst cheaper for very infrequent peaks but less predictable latency under sustained spikes. for your pattern (regular spikes to 160 rps), reserved baseline + small burst pool is likely cheaper and more reliable.
15:30 Nina: how do autoscaling windows work? we need to avoid flapping - our events are short but frequent.
16:00 Priya: we can set aggressive scale-up (few seconds) but conservative scale-down (2-5 minutes) to avoid oscillation; also use predictive autoscaling based on event signals if you can send a webhook when an event is scheduled.
18:12 Jordan: let's sketch numbers. baseline 25 rps, say 1 instance of A100-equivalent reserved gives X throughput for model A (explicit numbers shared later). For safety maybe reserve capacity for 40 rps baseline to cover steady growth.
20:05 Alex: can you quantify tokens per second throughput for our short chat model vs long model? we can share traces after the call but i need a ballpark to understand GPU counts.
21:00 Priya: ballpark: for a 60-token generation on A100 with optimized runtime you might get ~12-20 qps per GPU depending on batching; for the 400-token workload, throughput drops to 1-3 qps per GPU. so baseline chat workload (25 rps) could be 2 GPUs reserved with some room; long jobs require separate sizing or background worker pool.
23:10 Samir: ok so baseline 2 GPUs, burst pool maybe 8 GPUs to hit 160 rps short chat peak?
23:30 Priya: yes with effective batching and prefix caching you can get higher effective throughput but we'll validate with your traces. also consider model quantization (4-bit) for burst variants to increase capacity at lower cost with small quality impact.
25:00 Jordan: we should also align on model variants. AlphaTek wants model X-Inst (higher quality). fallback to X-Base quantized is acceptable during extreme load.
27:15 Elena: product question: how do we measure quality regression during fallback? we need guardrails.
28:00 Priya: recommend running a small evaluation set of 200 golden prompts each day during the POC and capture generation quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE is less relevant for chat, so human eval on a sample and automated heuristics like prompt-likelihood delta). We'll share an eval harness.
30:05 Alex: ok benchmark plan sounds good. what about network and region fallbacks? our users are US-centric but we have EU customers.
31:10 Priya: you can specify regional routing policies; for bursts we can spin up in multiple regions but costs will be higher. fallback to another region should be last resort and with a note about increased latency.
33:00 Nina: security questions: do we need VPC peering or a VPN for the POC? we prefer VPC if we can keep traffic internal for traces.
34:15 Jordan: for POC we can do a private deployment preview via VPC peering, or a hosted private link. We'll propose two options in the doc: hosted with strict retention and private VPC peering.
35:40 Samir: what's the SLA for reserved capacity?
36:00 Jordan: reserved capacity comes with higher uptime guarantees and priority access to burst pool, we'll share the SLA tiers; for POC it's usually best-effort but we can contract a short commitment if you want guaranteed latency windows.
37:25 Alex: any pitfalls with our KV cache approach? we store per-convo cache externally; we want co-location for low latency.
38:00 Priya: co-locating KV cache or using Redwood's prefix caching will save a lot of token compute. We can instrument cache hit rates in the pilot to tune batch sizes.
39:20 Jordan: let's move to the benchmark plan and timeline. Priya?
40:00 Priya: recommended POC steps: 1) share workload traces and test harness; 2) Redwood runs internal baseline benchmarks with same model variants; 3) joint run on AlphaTek test account with synthetic load to validate p95/p50 and cost per 1k preds; 4) iterate on autoscale policy and fallback thresholds. timeline: 2 weeks to run initial bench and adjustments, then 1 week of soak testing. so roughly 3-4 week POC.
44:10 Alex: sounds reasonable. are there resource constraints on your side for scheduling burst capacity?
44:30 Priya: for the pilot we can reserve a small burst pool; for larger bursts we may need advance notice or scheduled capacity reservation. we'll provide a recommended minimum reserved commit to make the economics work.
46:00 Samir: we need to ensure the cost model is clear - can you show cost per hour per GPU and cost per 1k predictions?
46:20 Jordan: yes we'll send a simple cost sheet mapping GPU types, reserved pricing, burst on-demand pricing, and example cost per 1k tokens for the two main workload types.
48:05 Elena: i'd like to confirm success criteria: p95 < 600ms for chat, p95 < 3s for long jobs, cost per 1k preds below X (tbd), no critical errors in 7-day soak.
49:10 Priya: we'll codify success criteria in the POC doc and include monitoring dashboards and eval hooks.
50:05 Alex: about fallback order, can you repeat the recommended sequence?
50:10 Jordan: recommended: 1) burst pool (same model, quantized variant) 2) lower-cost model variant same region 3) other region same model (with latency warning) 4) queue with priority based on session type. logs and metrics at each step for auditability.
51:05 Nina: what about canarying and rollback if quality drops after switch?
51:25 Priya: we can do canary traffic (5-10%) to a variant and monitor quality evals and latency before full roll. automatic rollback policies can be configured based on error rates or eval deltas.
51:50 Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc and links.

Transcript notes: occasional minor transcription errors, some speaker labels generic. Links referenced during call: benchmark spreadsheet (link: /redwood/benchmarks/alpha-poc), security whitepaper (link: /redwood/docs/security), pricing sheet (to be attached)

End of transcript.
